title: The debrief nobody wanted
note: Fictional patient. DRAFT pending clinical sign-off. Doses and energies are quoted from the 2025 AHA guidelines (and the ERC where named) for recognition; your unit protocol, crash-cart stock and the attending nephrologist come first. Simulation success is an educational result, not a prediction of patient survival.
intro: After a 25-minute resuscitation ending in transfer with ROSC, the team in Pampanga is exhausted. During the event: two physicians gave conflicting orders for a minute; one epinephrine dose was given twice; the watcher joined compressions and another patient’s pressure fell unnoticed; the patient’s daughter waited alone. A senior nurse says, “Let us just go back to work.” You are the charge nurse.

choices.text: Yes, ten minutes now, systems not people, using the five questions and the recorder’s sheet.
choices.feedback: A structured debrief is associated with better learning; fear of blame is why it needs structure.
The lessons are lost and the same failures recur.
choices.then: You hold a short debrief at shift end instead.

n2.prompt: The conflicting orders. What is the fix?

choices.text: A leadership handover script (“summary, I am taking the lead, you have the lead”) owned by the Dialysis Clinical Head and rehearsed in the next drill.
choices.feedback: System fix with an owner and a date.

choices.text: Tell the junior physician to stay quiet next time.
choices.feedback: Blaming a person leaves the system unchanged.
choices.then: The team agrees on a handover script instead.

choices.text: Closed-loop orders to named people and a recorder who calls doses due; owned by the head nurse and practiced in every drill.
choices.feedback: Orders to the room cause doubled and missed doses.

choices.text: A sign on the cart saying “check before giving.”
“The watcher never joins” added to the shift huddle (charge nurse); a staff member or social worker assigned to families during any code, with supported presence if policy allows.
choices.feedback: Other patients and families need named people.

choices.text: Nothing to change; it was a busy day.

end.title: 11:20 a.m.
end.text: Three changes, three owners, three dates, and a drill booked for next month. The action list goes on the notice board.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Debrief every event, about systems, not people.
  • Fix with owners and dates: leadership script, closed-loop orders, watcher rule, family support.
